rounds.restatement: Add a FENCE block and a fence filter that wrap content in a backtick code fence. The fence is sized to be longer than any backtick run inside the content, takes an optional lang from a quoted string or a variable path, drops one leading and one trailing line break, and ends with a line break after the closing fence. Add a heading_offset=N filter that shifts ATX headings outside fenced code, clamped to levels 1-6. Give escape_md an inline mode and a block mode, where block also neutralises line-start structure. Wire all of this through the lexer, parser, interpreter, analyze, spec and the standalone-line rule. An unclosed FENCE is a located syntax-error and FENCE counts toward maxDepth. Plain escape_md output and every existing test expectation stay unchanged, and no runtime dependency is added. The point is prompt-shaped output from a deterministic, no-eval core in which data cannot break the markdown structure the template author intended.
rounds.brief_mismatch:
The frozen test 'standalone on: a FENCE tag sharing its line with text is not removed' expected "a ```
x
``` b
". That contradicts c1 and the contract, which put a line break after the closing fence. The builder's corrected expectation is right on the merits, but it collides with m1 and with the rule that changing a frozen test is a deviation. The lead amended the manifest for it, so it is recorded here and as a drift finding, not as a fix request.

findings.title: A large value makes render throw a RangeError, because fence sizing spreads every backtick run into Math.max

serves.scenario: A FENCE body with about 130k backtick runs (a 260 KB value, well under maxOutputChars of 1,000,000) overflows the call stack in Math.max(...runs). The FENCE block lets a raw RangeError escape render(), which promises that template and data problems never throw. The fence filter returns a misleading type-error, 'Maximum call stack size exceeded', instead of the fenced value. Either way, valid input within the limits gets no c1 output.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c1: FENCE outputs a fence longer than the longest backtick run in its body)
findings.reproduction: render('{{FENCE}}${{b}}{{END_FENCE}}', {b: '`a'.repeat(130000)}, {standaloneLines:false}) throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. render('${{ b | fence }}', same data) returns ok:false with type-error 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. With 100000 repeats both still succeed. Smallest fix: find the longest run with a loop or reduce over body.match(/`+/g) instead of spreading into Math.max.
findings.label: f1

findings.title: A lang value from data can contain a line break or a backtick and break the fence or close it early

serves.scenario:
Goal-critical question 'can any body make the fence close early?': the body cannot, but lang is written raw onto the opening fence line. With {{FENCE lang=l}} and l = "md
```

```

x
```
". The fence closes on line 2, '# injected' renders as a real heading, and the body escapes the code block. A lang containing a backtick ("a`b") makes the opening line an invalid backtick fence in CommonMark, so the body is not fenced at all. Data controls whether the fence holds, which defeats the purpose of an auto-sized fence.

```

". render('{{FENCE lang=l}}# x{{END_FENCE}}', {l: 'a`b'}) returns "```a`b
# x
```
", which is not a valid fence. Smallest fix: in fenceLang, and in the fence filter, make a lang that contains a line break or a backtick a type-error at the FENCE tag or the variable.

serves.scenario: The value line '```js``` text' is inline code: a backtick fence's info string may not contain backticks. heading_offset treats it as an unclosed fence opener, so every later heading in the value is left unshifted. That violates 'shifts every ATX heading line'.

findings.title: Indented ATX headings (one to three leading spaces) are not shifted, although indented fences are recognised

serves.scenario: '  # h' is an ATX heading in CommonMark, but heading_offset leaves it alone, while the fence detector accepts up to three spaces of indent. The contract defines a heading as '#' followed by a space, so this meets the letter of c4; it is noted for the lead.

findings.title: heading_offset skips ATX headings indented by one to three spaces, though its own fence detection honours that indent

serves.scenario: c4 says heading_offset shifts every ATX heading line. In CommonMark an ATX heading may be indented by up to three spaces, and the filter's own fence detection accepts that indent (/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/). The heading rewrite only matches /^(#{1,6}) /, so a drafted value with ' # Notes' or '   ## Detail' keeps its level while the headings around it shift. The resulting document hierarchy is wrong (a sub-heading can end up above its parent). A tab after the hashes ('#	Title') is skipped the same way.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c4: shifts every ATX heading line)
findings.reproduction:
render('${{ v | heading_offset=1 }}', { v: ' # indented
   ## three
# top' }, { standaloneLines: false }).output is ' # indented
   ## three
## top'. The expected output is ' ## indented
   ### three
## top'. Smallest fix: match /^( {0,3})(#{1,6})(?=[ 	])/ in the rewrite and keep the captured indent.
findings.label: f7
